explorations.title: Scaling on versus off at the default inputs
explorations.instruction: scaling is turned off, q11, q12, q21, q22, k11, k12, k21, k22, v1 and v2 keep their defaults 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 10 and 20.
explorations.observe: The score matrix A and the weight matrix w stay at 0.5 in every entry in both settings, so the output readout keeps the rows 15 and 15; the raw dot-product matrix S is unchanged.
explorations.why: Raw dot products are identical in the two settings and are 0 off the diagonal, so the off-diagonal scores are 0 with and without scaling; the diagonal score 1 becomes 1/sqrt(2) when scaling is on. Both score matrices have equal entries within each row, so each row of the softmax is uniform and each output row is the average 0.5*10 + 0.5*20 = 15.

explorations.title: One dominant key with scaling on
explorations.instruction: scaling is turned on and k12 is raised to 100, while q11, q12, q21, q22, k11, k21, k22, v1 and v2 keep their defaults 1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 10 and 20.
explorations.observe: Row 1 of the weight readout is dominated by its second entry, with w[1][1] = 0, and output row 1 reads 20; row 2 of the weights and output row 2 are untouched.
explorations.why: S[1][2] = q11*k12 + q12*k22 = 100 while S[1][1] = 1, so after dividing by sqrt(2) the row-1 score gap is about 70; the shifted exponential of the smaller score is negligible, giving weight near 1 to key 2 and output row 1 equal to 1*v1 + 0*v2 evaluated at the unchanged row-2 weights.
